outline.description: This chapter establishes the legislative context surrounding the dispute, detailing the powers of the Office of Special Counsel (OSC) under both the Civil Service Reform Act and FOIA. It traces the factual timeline of America First Legal Foundation's (AFL) attempts to secure information regarding email searches, leading to OSC's refusal to investigate and the subsequent litigation path through the district court.
subtopics: AFL's Request for Emails and Subsequent Litigation Strategy
District Court Rulings: Error Finding versus Dismissal Based on Discretion

outline.chapter_title: Threshold Issue: Article III Standing Requirements
outline.description: Before addressing the merits of statutory interpretation, this chapter analyzes why the appellate court prioritized Article III standing. It defines the constitutional 'case or controversy' requirement and outlines the elements of injury-in-fact, causation, and redressability, specifically examining how these standards shift when a plaintiff alleges only a 'procedural right.'
subtopics: 'Case or Controversy' Requirement in Federal Courts
Three Prongs of Standing: Injury, Causation, Redressability
"Procedural Right" Doctrine and Relaxed Standards for Imminence/Redressability
Distinction Between Abstract Rights and Concrete Interests Affected by Procedure
